title: Reaching the second phase from the start
statement: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, let $x,y$ be Boolean words, and let $t_1\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose $M_1$ computes $y$ from $x$ in exactly $t_1$ steps. Then there are a time $a\le t_1+|y|+2$, a position of the physical input head on $x$, and contents and head positions for the left tape block such that the buffered composition, run from its initial configuration on $x$ for $a$ steps, is the second-phase configuration embedding of $M_2$'s initial configuration on input $y$, with boundary tag true and those chosen physical head position and left-block data.
hypotheses_covered: $M_1,M_2$ are finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet
replaced:
Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be machines over the Boolean alphabet with finitely many
states, and suppose that $M_1$, on input $x$, halts within $t_1$ steps with
output $y$.  Then there exist a step count $a \le t_1 + \abs{y} + 2$, a
position $p$ of the physical input head over $x$, and contents and head
positions for the left tape block, such that running the buffered sequential
composition of $M_1$ and $M_2$ for $a$ steps from its initial configuration
on $x$ yields the second-phase embedding of the initial configuration of
$M_2$ on virtual input $y$, with arrival tag true, physical position $p$, and
that inactive left-block data.
